title: Junior Platform Engineer Cohort Launch Playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for piloting a cohort-style hiring and onboarding program for Junior Platform Engineers (JPE). The intent is to intake 6 new hires as a single cohort every quarter, accelerate their time to first meaningful project, and create repeatable evaluation signals for hiring calibration and mentor load planning.

High-level goals:
- Reduce new JPE time-to-first-deploy from 12 weeks to 6 weeks.
- Surface top-of-cohort talent ready for IC2/IC3 within 6 months.
- Standardize interview signals so hiring decisions are consistent across interviewers.
- Build low-friction mentor pairings and a shared shadow-lab to limit SRE/Platform team disruption.

Cohort model summary:
- Size: target 6 hires per cohort (min 4, max 8).
- Duration of structured program: 12 weeks (intensive), followed by 3-month leveling runway.
- Format: blended async learning + twice-weekly cohort workshops + 1:1 mentor rotations.
- Intake cadence: quarterly (Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4) pilot in Q2 2026.

Hiring plan (timeline and responsibilities):
- Week -8 to -6: Sourcing push + hiring manager approval for cohort positions. Recruiter to open 6 reqs phased as a single cohort job posting.
- Week -6 to -3: Screen and phone loop. Recruiter and hiring manager to shortlist 12–18 candidates for on-site loop.
- Week -3 to 0: Interview loops (see rubric below). Final offers extended by Week 0.
- Offer cadence: staggered over 48 hours to enable alignment with compensation committee; target acceptance window 7 business days.
- Onboarding slot booking: Hiring manager to reserve buddy/mentor calendar blocks for first 6 weeks before offers accepted.

Interview rubric (compact, for JPE cohort only) — single-page signals for interviewers:
1) Systems reasoning (weight 30%)
   - Look for: ability to decompose a system design problem, tradeoffs, and failure modes.
   - Red flags: no concrete failure scenarios, inability to justify backups or observability choices.

2) Debugging and incident triage (weight 25%)
   - Look for: methodical approach, use of logs/metrics, hypothesis-driven triage.
   - Practical task: given a short incident vignette simulate triage steps and next actions.

3) Scripting and automation (weight 20%)
   - Look for: comfort writing small scripts or shell pipelines, basic infra-as-code knowledge.
   - Acceptable techs: Python/Bash/Small HCL snippets.

4) Collaboration and communication (weight 15%)
   - Look for: clear async documentation style, ability to escalate appropriately, stakeholder empathy.

5) Cultural fit and growth mindset (weight 10%)
   - Look for: curiosity, receptiveness to feedback, pragmatic prioritization.

Scoring guidance:
- Use a 1–4 scale per category (1 = needs work, 4 = strong).
- Minimum pass threshold: average >= 2.5 and no category below 2.
- Panel calibration: hiring managers and recruiter to run a 30-minute calibration session after first 8 interviews.

Sample interview loop structure (3–4 interviewers, 90–120m total):
- 25m Systems reasoning + design prompt (take-home optional)
- 20m Debugging vignette (live)
- 20m Scripting/automation live exercise (pair-programming or whiteboard)
- 15m Culture/behavior + Q&A
- Debrief: hidden 10–15m scoring and immediate pass/no-pass recommendation.

Onboarding checklist (first 30 days — cohort-adapted):
Before day 1 (owner: People Ops + IT):
- Hardware shipped and received (laptop, power, accessories).
- Access secured: corporate email, VPN, Okta groups, GitHub, CI dashboards, cloud console (least privilege staging).
- Slack channels pre-joined: #platform-cohort-<cohort-number>, #oncall-sandbox, #infra-announcements.

Day 0–7 (orientation + safety):
- Day 0: Welcome + company values session (People Ops) + introductions to platform team.
- Day 1–3: Shadow lab orientation: read sandbox README, run through a curated set of 6 micro-tasks (start/stopping test clusters, viewing metrics, rolling back a staged deploy).
- Day 4: Security & compliance micro-cert (30m walkthrough + quiz).
- Day 5–7: Pair with assigned mentor on a tiny cleanup ticket and ship a doc PR to internal onboarding repo.

Week 2–4 (ramp + ownership):
- Week 2: Small ownerable task: own a non-critical scheduled job (pager-free). Deliverable: runbook doc + metrics dashboard.
- Week 3: Code review rotations: each cohort member reviews 2 PRs and receives 2 PR reviews.
- Week 4: Mini-project kickoff: a 2-week scoped infra improvement (e.g., add informer metrics to an internal service). Present plan at cohort demo.

Week 5–8 (real projects + oncall introduction):
- Introduce lightweight oncall shadow shifts (no primary pager).
- Rotate pair-programming on a production-safe rollback or capacity test.
- Mentor check-ins twice weekly.

Evaluation and checkpoints:
- End of week 4: formal checkpoint — hiring manager + mentor + people ops review progress.
- End of week 8: competency review against rubric; possible leveling recommendation for fast movers.
- End of week 12: graduation demo to platform leadership, decision tree for promotion trajectory or extension.

Mentor program mechanics:
- Mentor ratio: 1 mentor per 2–3 cohort members for first 8 weeks. Mentors are volunteer senior engineers from platform teams with 4–6 hours/week commitment.
- Mentor prep kit: 1-page mentoring playbook (how to give feedback, suggested shadow tasks, escalation points).
- Mentor stipend: $500 one-time honorarium per mentor per cohort (pilot budget).

Shadow-lab and learning resources (practical stack):
- Sandboxes pre-provisioned with ephemeral clusters (k8s), a metrics stack (Prometheus/Grafana), and a mini-logging pipeline.
- Curated micro-learning list: internal runbooks, three short SRE videos, two small terraform exercises.
- Starter tickets catalog: ~20 SRE-safe tickets labelled JPE-starter ready.

Risk register (top immediate risks):
- Mentor burnout if not properly compensated or scheduled. Mitigation: cap commitments and rotate mentors.
- Acceptance churn for offers during competitive markets. Mitigation: shorten offer window and improve candidate experience with cohort-specific benefits.
- Insufficient sourcing volume for diverse slate. Mitigation: partner with university/private bootcamp channels and allocate dedicated sourcing quota.

Metrics to track (success signals):
- Time-to-first-successful-deploy (target <= 6 weeks).
- Fraction of cohort achieving IC2 readiness signal by 6 months (target >= 50%).
- Hiring funnel conversion: screens -> on-site -> offers -> accepts (target 30% accept rate for offers extended).
- Mentor satisfaction NPS after cohort (target >= 60).

Operational checklist for the pilot (owners):
- Recruiter: create cohort job posting and sourcing plan (Due: -8w).
- Hiring manager: reserve mentor calendar and finalize initial tickets (Due: -4w).
- People Ops: assemble welcome packet and schedule orientation sessions (Due: -2w).
- SRE/Platform leads: provision sandboxes and starter tickets (Due: -3w).

Open questions for leadership before Q2 pilot:
- Approve budget for mentor stipends and sandbox infra costs?
- Minimum acceptance threshold for running cohort vs. postponing?
- Are managers willing to commit mentor time budgets and backlog accommodations?

Next steps (short):
- Review with People Ops leadership (this week).
- Recruiter to validate sourcing channels and commit to outreach plan by end of month.
- Run a mock calibration with 3 internal interviews to test rubric clarity.

Notes to self / working items:
- Consider light gamification for cohort (badges for milestones).
- Prepare a short FAQ for candidates about cohort format.
- Draft a 6-month competency ladder specific to platform cohort progression.

Appendix (links and templates):
- Quick mentor playbook template: /onboarding/mentor-playbook.md (internal repo)
- Starter ticket template: Jira: JIRA-PLT-STARTER-TEMPLATE
- Example runbook checklist: runbook-template.md

End of document. This remains a living draft; comments welcome in the doc and please flag items that need immediate leadership review.
